definitions.explanation: Positive: done in an impressive, admirable way
Can emphasize completeness, sometimes of a failure

examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}に{見事|みごと}に{勝|か}った。
{彼|かれ}は{難|むずか}しい{課題|かだい}を{見事|みごと}にやり{遂|と}げた。
examples.english: He accomplished the difficult task brilliantly.

examples.japanese: {桜|さくら}が{見事|みごと}に{咲|さ}き{誇|ほこ}っている。
examples.english: The cherry blossoms are blooming magnificently.

examples.japanese: {予想|よそう}が{見事|みごと}に{外|はず}れた。
{計画|けいかく}は{見事|みごと}に{失敗|しっぱい}した。
{彼|かれ}の{嘘|うそ}は{見事|みごと}に{見抜|みぬ}かれた。
examples.english: His lie was completely seen through.

notes:
The adverbial form of {見事|みごと} (na-adjective meaning splendid/magnificent). Has two distinct uses: expressing admiration for something done impressively well, or emphasizing the completeness or thoroughness of something — including negative outcomes.

USAGE:
With positive verbs (sense 1), it praises the quality of an achievement. With negative outcomes (sense 2), it emphasizes how completely or thoroughly something went wrong, often with a touch of irony.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見事|みごと}に{成功|せいこう}する: to succeed brilliantly
- {見事|みごと}に{失敗|しっぱい}する: to fail spectacularly
- {見事|みごと}に{外|はず}れる: to be completely off the mark
- {見事|みごと}に{咲|さ}く: to bloom magnificently
- {見事|みごと}にやり{遂|と}げる: to accomplish brilliantly

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {立派|りっぱ}に: admirably, splendidly — similar but only used positively
- {完全|かんぜん}に: completely — neutral emphasis on completeness without the "impressively" nuance
